attributes.provenance: src/game/mb/mb_tree.c::MBTreeInit (worktree GDL-Claude-FlipClosest, work_claim.flip-closest.20260831.v1, commits a28a2a51a + 79df14a60). Target frame 40, ours 48, insns 310/310 with EVERY non-frame instruction already identical. A full (r1) census of both streams (fnasm target vs --ours, filtered to `(r1)`) returned FIVE rows on each side and they were all linkage: stw r0,4(r1); stwu; stmw/lmw r29; lwz r0. Zero local-slot references in either version, so the 20B (target) / 28B (ours) local area is entirely dead reservation. Collapsing three never-simultaneously-live MBTreeNode* locals (node1/node2/node3, each stored to its own global and used immediately, never read later) into ONE reused local removed exactly 8 nominal bytes and took real 10 -> 0 in a single probe. Independently confirmed in the opposite direction in the same function: replacing an `extern const f32` load with the equivalent pool literal 1e37f ADDED exactly 8 bytes back, and deleting the then-redundant `f32 default_scale` local removed them again. Cross-checked against src/game/ps2/fakelib.c::sDvdReadSync, whose independent 2026-08-30 park recorded the identical signature (dead local area, 20 target vs 28 ours) and explicitly concluded that no law in the corpus addressed it.

subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: MWCC sizes a function's local area from DECLARED locals in an early pass, and does NOT shrink it when register allocation later leaves every one of them fully register-resident. A function can therefore carry a local area that no instruction ever reads or writes, and a pure frame-size delta with an otherwise instruction-identical body is closed by changing WHAT IS DECLARED, not by chasing spills or register colors. DIAGNOSTIC FIRST, because it is cheap and decisive: dump the (r1) rows of both streams (fnasm <unit> <fn> --diff and --ours, filter to `(r1)`). If the ONLY (r1) rows on both sides are the linkage set - stw r0,4(r1), stwu, stmw/lmw, lwz r0 - then the entire local area is dead nominal reservation and no store-placement, spill, or slot-displacement theory can apply; go straight to the declaration list. LEVER: collapse locals that are never simultaneously live into one reused variable. Three MBTreeNode* declarations, each assigned then consumed immediately with no later read, cost 8 nominal bytes over the single reused local the original used, and merging them closed a 48-vs-40 frame in ONE probe. This is the constructive complement to claim.law.stack-slots-descend-in-declaration-order.20260831.v1: that law governs the ORDER and displacement of slots that are actually referenced, this one governs the SIZE of the block when none of them are. COROLLARY, measured in both directions on the same function: constant materialization form also buys nominal space. Loading a float through an `extern const f32` symbol costs no local slot, while spelling the same value as a pool literal (1e37f) cost 8 nominal bytes and re-inflated the frame; the space came back by deleting the local that had held the value. So when a literal-for-symbol substitution is forced for other reasons (see the TU-flip pool law), expect to pay a nominal slot and budget a declaration to remove. CAUTION, measured negative: this is NOT a simple byte-sum you can always drive. On fakelib.c::sDvdReadSync removing one 4-byte local measured EXACTLY neutral (the frame is 8-byte aligned, so a 4-byte reduction can round away entirely - reduce in 8-byte steps), and removing the `base` pointer local was strongly negative (real 10 -> 80, insns 87 -> 99) because that local was load-bearing: it holds a global's address live across several uses, and deleting it re-materializes the lis/addi pair at every use. Only merge locals that are genuinely dead after their last read, and never one that anchors a shared address web.
